title: Willis Young builds the New Orleans Strutters dance band in Minneapolis
summary: On the show Young rehearses a dance band, books a dance in Minneapolis, rents a big house and builds an 11-piece band that played the Radisson Hotel.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: So you and Lester and Jones were in that other show with Mrs. Young.
But Mr. Young was not going around with you?
Yeah, he was there. I told you, he left the show and turned it over to Kitchen. He'd taken us with

him over to Mrs. Young's show. Then, when we stayed on that show, well, we got about three or four more guys in the band. James was with us. Curtis Oliver. Anyway, we had trombone and two saxophones, and trumpet. So we rehearsed on the show, while we was traveling. He was getting this band together. And he booked a dance in Minneapolis. Well, we went there and played the dance, and we stayed in Minneapolis. We stayed in Minneapolis all that winter, up until the next spring. We was headquarterin' out if there, He went there and rented a big house.

Yes. So we stayed there in Minneapolis. He had a big house for all the musicians where we stayed. A nice place to live. And he had a big room where we rehearsed. We rehearsed practically every day. Then after he stayed there, he got this big band together, 11 pieces. He got some guys out of... That picture, you know, that I showed you. That's the band that he got together in Minneapolis. Then he started booking jobs... That's where that was taken, in the Radisson Hotel. So we played there. See, he was booking jobs like mad for that band, because the New Orleans Strutters was something kind of new...
